summary: The article accurately explains the CBDT's new crypto reporting guidance, its alignment with OECD CARF, and its implications for Indian investors, including existing tax rates and loss set-off rules.

claims.claim: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has issued guidance aligning India's crypto reporting with global OECD standards.
claims.note: The CBDT has issued a guidance note to operationalise India's crypto-asset reporting framework in line with the OECD's global standards.

claims.claim: It does not introduce new taxes on crypto assets; existing tax laws remain unchanged.
claims.note: For investors, however, there is no change in taxation.

claims.claim: The existing tax provisions for Virtual Digital Assets (VDAs) include a 30% tax on gains and 1% TDS on certain transactions.
claims.note: The existing 30% tax on gains from Virtual Digital Assets (VDAs) and 1% TDS on eligible transactions continue to apply.

claims.claim: Under current VDA tax rules, losses from one VDA cannot be set off against gains from another VDA, nor against any other income.
claims.note: As per Section 115BBH, losses incurred in crypto cannot be offset against any income, including gains from cryptocurrency.

claims.claim: Crypto-Asset Service Providers (CASPs) are responsible for collecting relevant information from their users and reporting it to the Indian tax authorities.
claims.note: The note gives guidance to Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Providers (RCASPs) for compliance with the reporting obligations under section 509 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, and under Rules 241 to 244 and Form 167 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026.

claims.claim: The reporting period for crypto exchanges will be each calendar year starting after the January 1, 2026. The required statements will have to be filed by May 31 of the calendar year following the year to which the information relates.
